judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the Elementor hero background video: a YouTube iframe (controls=0, role=presentation) inside div.elementor-background-video-container. On the live page both the iframe and that container have pointer-events: none, so a mouse user cannot interact with it either; there is no functionality here that only a pointer can reach, which is what 2.1.1 is about (a missing pause control would be a 2.2.2 question, not this one). The 'never reached' claim also does not hold: in my own headless Edge Tab walk at 1280x800 focus entered the iframe twice (YouTube's caption window and its 'Mostrar controles do player' button). The probe's network guard blocked YouTube's player requests (youtubei/v1/player) and its screenshot shows a blank hero, so the frame had nothing focusable in the probe run: an artefact of the probe environment.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The header logo link (a.elementor-clickable wrapping the logo image, href to the home page). I looked for a reason it could pass: the site CSS gives it outline: 3px solid black on focus, but the anchor is display: inline around block children, so the outline is not painted. With the welcome modal removed from the live page, Tab-focusing versus blurring the logo changed 0 px within 20 px of it, and a screenshot of it focused shows no ring, underline or other change. This is not caused by the modal (it fails without it), and the accessibility toolbar offers no focus-highlight mode, so no mode of operation shows its focus: 2.4.7 fails.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'O Museu' submenu toggle (div role=button) in the main menu, focused at Tab 15. The obscurer is the welcome popup #premium-modal-cbfd80b (role=dialog, no aria-modal). Its page settings say trigger=pageload, delay 3, so it opens without any user action. It never takes focus (its close button is about the 30th Tab stop) and does not close when focus moves behind it. I checked whether the element could still show through: the backdrop is rgba(0,0,0,0.5), but the element at 369-484 x 87-141 sits under the opaque white panel (rgb(255,255,255), 290-990 x 75-725 px at 1280x800). Every point I tested hit the panel, and the probe found that painting the element changed 0 px. The Note 2 exception covers only content the user opened. The Understanding document says content that appears without user initiation must not keep the focused item from being visible, and that a dialog-like overlay which neither takes focus nor constrains it is at risk. Nothing makes this pass, so 2.4.11 fails.
